listing.name: WIP - Beyond The Black: a BSG and The Expanse inspired hard sci fi mod
listing.summary: Removes shields and special ship systems, replacing them with a focus on armor, flux management, and active countermeasures.
listing.aiSummary: Removes shields and special ship systems, replacing them with a focus on armor, flux management, and active countermeasures.

description:
A while back I wondered if Starsector could work with hard sci fi rules we see in Battlestar Galactica and The Expanse TV shows. So I created this mod to test it out, and it turned out pretty good.

This mod is basically the two shows mixed together, with a few Starsector things added in as well as flavor.

DONWLOAD

This is very much a work in progress, and I am, for now at least, taking a break from actually working on it. I got burned out by it a bit, so I need a rest. I figured before I do take that rest that I might as well release what I’ve got so far, so that fans of BSG and The Expanse can enjoy it as well.

Right now, all that is really implement completely is the combat system, with the new ships and weapons.

What you can do now is start a new campaign (no matter the start, you will receive all of the faction ships) and play around with the new ships and weapons in the simulator

(press “r”, select your ship, then press “n”). If you don’t want to see vanilla ships in the simulator, then you will have to rename your sim_opponents.csv to something else (like “backup_sim_opponents.csv”) your starsector-core\data\campaign folder. Unfortunately I cannot prevent this file from loading on my own through the mod functionality that is available natively.

I did wish to implement a fully functioning campaign, with new perks, hull mods, factions, etc, but it’s just so much work to do still that I put it on hold.

If anyone does wish to work on it further on their own, go right ahead, I’ll be glad to see it. If anyone wants to use any parts of this mod for their own mod, also go right ahead.

So here is what I changed.

SpoilerNo shields. For any ship. Ships have to rely purely on armor for survival.

5 custom factions (+1 pirate faction), all with their own set of unique ships.

No special ship systems. Instead, every ship gets a modified burn drive that gives them about 2-3x their regular top speed, at the expense of flux buildup. Capital ships benefit the most.

Drifting is now performed at 80% of top speed. Ships can only achieve top speed by accelerating with their engines. This means escaping by going backwards or sideways will be much harder now.

No hard flux venting. Because the AI can’t use it with this new concept and it doesn’t really fit in with the setting. Instead you have to rely on passive venting and manage your flux carefully.

Missiles are much faster than in vanilla, and very devastating. In fact, the game now revolves around creating a situation where missiles overwhelm the opponent’s anti-missile capabilities.

Point defense weapons are an absolute must for any ship, but are also way more effective than in vanilla.

Instead of ship systems, ships have active countermeasures against missiles that are deployed automatically. These come in the form of flares or a barrage of flak at a set distance that acts as essentially an anti-missile shield.

Two factions use special shield alternatives that are taken from vanilla, but modified. Phasing and damper field.

Ship can now repair at the cost of their combat rating. About 2% for each point of CR. The repair is capped to about 70%, give or take (faction based).

Increased range for all weapon types. The fight now starts at 8000 units with a barrage of missiles. Max camera zoom has been increased.

All vanilla ships and weapons are hidden. The variety of weapons has been greatly decreased, but every single weapon has utility now. Weapon choice now matters greatly, and there is no universal “best” weapon you’ll want to use on every ship.

Completely remade damage decals. Ship damage decals now reflect the nature of the weapons in this mod. That is, ships will now look like they’re peppered by large and small holes and scorch marks.

Changed battle backgrounds. You can delete the backgrounds folder if you don’t like them.[close]

Factions

SpoilerThere is no real lore to the factions you see in my mod. They’re mainly here to add flavor. I tried to make them all a bit unique in their own way. All the faction, with the exception of pirates, are named after the colors their ships are painted in.

BLU

These are the all-rounders. Their ships are well balanced, and generally well equipped to take on any other faction. They rely on railguns a bit more than most of the other factions to deal damage, but other than that pretty unremarkable.

GRN

Their ships are large and bulky, which stretches their armor thin. That said, they excel at building carriers, and their capital ships carry more wings than the other factions.

RED

Their ships tend to be a bit smaller, but very well armored. They excel at close combat, but are limited by the fact that they do not use heavy flux producing weapons. As such, they are limited by the ammo pool of their cannons and PDCs, and will suffer ammo shortages the longer the fight drags on.

YLO

This is the stealth faction. All their ships can phase in and out of harm’s way and as such are extremely hard to actually catch. They do not field any fighter or gunship wings, instead relying on their frigates and corvettes to surround and ambush their enemies. Their missiles are faster and better armed, and all their ships equipped with railguns. Their ships are small and fragile, so damage avoidance is crucial for them.

PRP

Extremely high tech faction. Their smaller ships are well armored and pack a serious punch, while their larger ships tend to be more fragile but come equipped with a damper field defense system that reduces incoming damage by 90% when active, which gives them remarkable ability to tank damage. Their cruisers come equipped with an ion cannon that disable ships from long range, leaving them defenseless against a barrage of missiles.

Pirates

A group of ragtag bandits that steal civilian ships and turn them into warships. Their ships don’t pose much of a challenge to real warships, but they should still not be underestimated, as their ships do carry dangerous missiles.[close]

Ships

SpoilerFrigate

The smallest ship capable of independent patrol duties. Quite fragile, but very fast. Mainly intended for anti smuggling and anti piracy duties in the trade lanes.

Heavy Frigate

An upgrade to the frigate, it’s got more armor and armaments, but at the cost of speed. Intended for independent anti piracy operations, as well as privateering. Often operates in small wolf packs of frigates or as an escort for destroyers.

Destroyer

Fast, well armored and well armed, it can take on any pirate, and can hold it’s own against multiple enemies. Can get overwhelmed fast if not careful with it’s positioning.  Intended for anti piracy, privateering, civilian escort and anti frigate combat. Often operates in small groups of other destroyers and heavy frigates.

Heavy Destroyer

The upgraded version of the destroyer, and a true force to be reckoned with. With the right captain, the heavy destroyer can take on even a cruiser and come up on top. That said, it’s lack of speed can hurt it against lighter ships, especially fighters, which might overwhelm it’s defenses, leaving it defenseless against missiles.

Cruiser

The smallest ship capable of housing other ships. Well armed, and fast for a capital ship, it’s main draw back is the lackluster armor. It’s small hanger is usually occupied by a frigate. They are usually found either alone or with a heavy destroyer escort, operating as forward reconnaissance.

Heavy Cruiser

Member of the big boy club. Carries a small fleet of wings as well as impressive armor and armament. They are the only ships besides battleships to have a large weapons mount, which give them devastating strike capability.

Battleship

The pride of any navy. The Battleship is the largest ship in the game, and also the slowest. It has enough firepower to take on an entire fleet of lesser ships, and still come out on top. Truly an impressive constructions, but also slow, and expensive. Only the BLU, GRN and RED posses the capability to build them.

[close]

Wings

SpoilerFighters

Fighters shoot down missiles, engage other fighters, hunt down gunships, chase after frigates and corvettes, and annoy capital ships. They are best used in combination with corvettes and gunships, as they lack the staying power or the firepower to replace either of those. Exceptionally useful in the later stages of the fight, once PDCs and flak start running into ammo issues, as they can deplete said defenses of ammo even faster, allowing friendly missiles to get through.

Gunships

Gunships are designed to deliver a high yield armored torpedo right on top of an enemy ship, within it’s flak shield. They are well armored, and well armed for their size, but lack maneuverability of fighters to engage in dogfights. As such, once their payload is released, they return to their mother ship to reload.

Corvettes

Corvettes are essentially frigates without all the space needed for independent patrols. As such, they are much smaller, but carry similar armament and armor. They defend other ships in the fleet, acting as screens against missiles, cannon and railgun shots, as well as fighter and gunship hunters. Extremely valuable for any capital ship to have. Their downside is that they cannot pursue enemy ships, as they can only defend friendly ships.[close]

Weapons

SpoilerThe weapons in this mod are very different than in the vanilla game. Overall, they have much longer ranges and are faster, and they also have replenishing ammunition stores.

Broadly, the weapons in this mod can be divided into several categories. Offensive vs defensive, energy vs ammo draining, and interceptable vs direct.

Point Defense Cannons (PDCs) are your main defense against missiles and fighters. Every ship has them, and they are indispensable. If the PDCs go down, you are in big trouble. There’s 2 type, the regular PDC relies on ammo, which it spends several times faster than it replenishes, so it has to be managed carefully, and the railgun PDC, which does not consume ammo, deals 2x more damage to armor, but generates 10x more flux. PDCs can be used offensively as well, though they will always prioritize missiles over enemy ships. They also get tricked by enemy flares.

Flak is an adjunct to PDCs, and creates an area of denial for missiles. It’s main downside is it’s poor accuracy, limited ammo pool and slow replenishment. Flak can also be used to fend of enemy fighters, though because it causes fragmentation damage it only does 0.25 damage to armor.

Missiles are the main damage dealers in this mod, but their application is limited by the enemy’s defensive capabilities. High explosive torpedoes strip away armor and cause heavy damage to the hull, plasma torpedoes cause ion damage and disable ship components and weapons, swarm torpedoes overload the enemy’s PDCs and anti fighter missiles hunt down enemy fighters. Most missile have very high range.

Cannons are low tech direct damage dealers that require very little flux to fire, but are limited by their ammo pool, which replenishes slower than it’s fired. As such, they lose their efficiency the longer the battle drags on. They cannot be intercepted, and generally have low to mid range.

Railguns are kinetic weapons that use electricity to propel a tungsten slug at incredible speeds, well above what a cannon is capable of. They require no ammo, but generate a ton of flux, and are therefore limited to ships that have good flux venting capacity. They have mid to high range.

aiDescription: Removes shields and special ship systems, replacing them with a focus on armor, flux management, and active countermeasures. Introduces faster, more devastating missiles and improved point defense systems, making combat heavily reliant on missile saturation and anti-missile defenses. Adds five unique factions with distinct ship designs, combat roles, and specialized abilities, along with new ship classes, wings, and weapon types that emphasize long-range engagements and tactical positioning.
